checkCodeProgram.source:
*** Epi Info AI foodborne Check Code tour
*** This bounded source exercises definitions plus Form, Page, Record, and Field events.
*** Import the packaged foodborne project, inspect and verify this source, then open Enter Data.

/* Legacy Epi Info Check Code commonly uses multiline comments like this one.
   Comments remain visible to the reviewer but do not become executable AST nodes. */

// Standard variables reset with the data-entry session.
DefineVariables
  DEFINE ReviewState STANDARD TEXTINPUT
  DEFINE ReviewNote STANDARD TEXTINPUT
  DEFINE ContinueReview STANDARD YN
End-DefineVariables

*** A bounded subroutine can be called from one or more event blocks.
Sub FlagImplausibleAge
  HIGHLIGHT age
  BEEP
  DIALOG "Age must be between 0 and 120 years." TITLETEXT="Age plausibility review"
End-Sub

*** Form events bracket the form session.
Form
  Before
    ASSIGN ReviewState = "Ready"
  End-Before
  After
    ENABLE case_status
  End-After
End-Form

*** Page events run only while their page is active.
Page EntryPage
  Before
    DIALOG "Continue reviewing this foodborne case?" ContinueReview YN TITLETEXT="Foodborne case review"
  End-Before
  After
    ENABLE onset_date
  End-After
End-Page

Page Clinical
  Before
    ENABLE onset_date onset_time hospitalization_date specimen_date interview_date
  End-Before
  After
    UNHIGHLIGHT onset_date
  End-After
End-Page

Page ExposureLocation
  Before
    ENABLE latitude longitude household_neighborhood
  End-Before
End-Page

*** Record events run before entry and after a successful save.
Record
  Before
    ALWAYS
      CLEAR onset_time
      UNHIGHLIGHT * EXCEPT age
    END
  End-Before
  After
    IF case_status = "Confirmed" THEN
      LET ReviewState = "Reviewed"
    ELSE-IF case_status = "Probable" THEN
      LET ReviewState = "Follow-up"
    ELSE
      LET ReviewState = "Pending"
    END-IF
    LET ReviewNote = "Transient review complete"
    UNDEFINE ReviewNote
  End-After
End-Record

*** Enter an existing ID, then leave the field to preview matching saved records.
*** The browser candidate never replaces the current draft or opens the match.
Field id
  After
    AUTOSEARCH id DISPLAYLIST id age sex case_status CONTINUENEW ALWAYS
  End-After
End-Field

*** Enter Confirmed, then leave Case Status to see highlight, required state, and GOTO.
Field case_status
  Before
    ENABLE case_status
  End-Before
  After
    IF case_status = "Confirmed" THEN
      HIGHLIGHT onset_date
      SET-REQUIRED onset_date
      ENABLE onset_date
      GOTO onset_date
    ELSE
      UNHIGHLIGHT onset_date
      SET-NOT-REQUIRED onset_date
    END-IF
  End-After
End-Field

*** Flag implausible ages while leaving plausible or blank values unhighlighted.
Field age
  After
    IF age < 0 OR age > 120 THEN
      CALL FlagImplausibleAge
    ELSE
      UNHIGHLIGHT age
    END-IF
  End-After
End-Field

*** Leaving a populated Onset Date reveals and enables Onset Time.
Field onset_date
  After
    IF NOT (onset_date = (.) OR onset_date = "") THEN
      UNHIDE onset_time
      ENABLE onset_time
    END-IF
  End-After
End-Field

*** Legacy GOTOPAGE makes the named page transition explicit and auditable.
Field interview_date
  After
    IF NOT (interview_date = (.) OR interview_date = "") THEN
      GOTOPAGE ExposureLocation
    END-IF
  End-After
End-Field

*** Record lifecycle effects are allowed only from a Command Button Click event.
*** SAVE-RECORD uses the same validation and audit-visible form workflow as the UI button.
Field save_record
  Click
    SAVE-RECORD
  End-Click
End-Field

programs.name: foodborne-classic-command-tour
programs.source:
*** Epi Info AI foodborne Classic Analysis command tour
*** Dataset: foodborne-outbreak-investigation.csv (96 records)
*** PARITY ACCEPTANCE TARGET - not yet a legacy-parity-verified demo program.
*** Choose Run Commands with no selection to execute this tour in source order.
*** As in Epi Info 7, highlighting one complete command or block first runs only
*** that selected source.

LIST ID Age Sex case_status onset_date

FREQ case_status

FREQ case_status STRATAVAR=Sex

MEANS Age

SET (.)="Not recorded"

SET MISSING=ON

TABLES vomiting Sex

SET MISSING=OFF

SET (.)="Missing"

TABLES potato_salad hamburger

TABLES potato_salad hamburger STRATAVAR=Sex

TABLES potato_salad case_status STRATAVAR=Sex STATISTICS=FISHER

*** Mechanical WEIGHTVAR demonstration only: Age is not a defensible survey weight
TABLES potato_salad case_status WEIGHTVAR=Age

*** Mechanical PSUVAR demonstration only: Household Neighborhood is a PSU proxy
TABLES potato_salad hamburger STRATAVAR=Sex WEIGHTVAR=Age PSUVAR=household_neighborhood OUTTABLE=PotatoHamburgerSurvey

TABLES potato_salad hamburger STRATAVAR=Sex case_status

SELECT case_status = "Confirmed" AND Age >= 18

FREQ Sex

CANCEL SELECT

SORT Age DESCENDING

LIST ID Age Sex case_status

CANCEL SORT

SUMMARIZE AverageAge :: AVG(Age) TO FoodborneAgeBySex STRATAVAR=Sex

GRAPH case_status GRAPHTYPE="Bar" TITLETEXT="Foodborne cases by status" XTITLE="Count" YTITLE="Case Status"

*** Legacy TABLES OUTTABLE: creates a session-local long-form table for later READ
TABLES potato_salad case_status STRATAVAR=Sex OUTTABLE=PotatoStatusBySex

*** Legacy GROUPVAR exposure expansion: one TABLES output per food field
DEFINE FoodExposures GROUPVAR potato_salad hamburger grilled_chicken

TABLES FoodExposures case_status OUTTABLE=FoodExposureStatusCounts

*** Mechanical CSF demonstration only: neighborhood is a PSU proxy and Age a test weight
FREQ case_status STRATAVAR=Sex WEIGHTVAR=Age PSUVAR=household_neighborhood OUTTABLE=CaseStatusSurvey

*** Mechanical Complex Sample Means demonstration only
*** OUTTABLE is a browser-adapted result table; desktop CSM leaves this control disabled
MEANS Age Sex STRATAVAR=case_status OUTTABLE=AgeBySexSurvey PSUVAR=household_neighborhood

*** NEW BRANCH - browser-native quality profile; not an Epi Info 7 command
EPIAI QUALITY *

*** Familiar IF / ELSE / END branch using Standard session variables only
*** Record-field IF execution remains fail-closed pending record-by-record parity
DEFINE ReviewLabel TEXTINPUT

DEFINE PriorityFlag YN

ASSIGN ReviewLabel = "Priority review"

IF ReviewLabel = "Priority review" THEN
  ASSIGN PriorityFlag = (+)
ELSE
  ASSIGN PriorityFlag = (-)
END

DIALOG "Review the foodborne outbreak analysis results." TITLETEXT="Foodborne outbreak review"

BEEP

ROUTEOUT "foodborne-command-tour.html" REPLACE

HEADER 1 "Foodborne outbreak command tour"

TYPEOUT "Canonical example: 96 submitted foodborne outbreak records."

CLOSEOUT

PRINTOUT

programs.comment: Foodborne Classic Analysis parity and new-branch command tour.

programs.name: foodborne-check-code-expressions
programs.source:
*** Epi Info AI foodborne Check Code expression and function tour
*** Candidate subset recovered from the legacy Enter grammar; verify before Apply.

DefineVariables
  DEFINE AgeDistance STANDARD NUMERIC
  DEFINE StatusLabel STANDARD TEXTINPUT
  DEFINE InterviewYear STANDARD NUMERIC
  DEFINE InterviewEpiWeek STANDARD NUMERIC
  DEFINE RootAge STANDARD NUMERIC
  DEFINE LogAge STANDARD NUMERIC
  DEFINE ReviewDate STANDARD DATEFORMAT
  DEFINE ReviewTime STANDARD TIMEFORMAT
  DEFINE ReviewHour STANDARD NUMERIC
  DEFINE DaysToInterview STANDARD NUMERIC
  DEFINE ReviewSummary STANDARD TEXTINPUT
  DEFINE SavedRecordCount STANDARD NUMERIC
  DEFINE IdentifierAvailable STANDARD YN
  DEFINE ReviewSystemDate STANDARD DATEFORMAT
  DEFINE ReviewSystemTime STANDARD TIMEFORMAT
  DEFINE ReviewOperator STANDARD TEXTINPUT
  DEFINE CapturedLatitude STANDARD NUMERIC
  DEFINE CapturedLongitude STANDARD NUMERIC
  DEFINE CapturedAltitude STANDARD NUMERIC
  DEFINE ReviewSampleNumber STANDARD NUMERIC
  DEFINE AgeTeachingZ STANDARD NUMERIC
  DEFINE AgeTeachingPercentile STANDARD NUMERIC
  DEFINE AdultReview STANDARD YN
End-DefineVariables

Record
  After
    // Arithmetic observes legacy precedence and ROUND uses midpoint-away-from-zero.
    ASSIGN AgeDistance = ROUND(ABS(age - 40) / 3, 2)

    // SUBSTRING is 1-based, STRLEN returns the character count, and & concatenates.
    ASSIGN StatusLabel = UPPERCASE(SUBSTRING(case_status, 1, 4)) & "-" & STRLEN(case_status)

    // Date extraction accepts an ISO YYYY-MM-DD value and remains missing when its input is missing.
    ASSIGN InterviewYear = YEAR(interview_date)
    ASSIGN InterviewEpiWeek = EPIWEEK(interview_date)

    // Browser dates and times use unambiguous ISO values; two-digit years retain legacy expansion.
    ASSIGN ReviewDate = NUMTODATE(26, 9, 23)
    ASSIGN ReviewTime = NUMTOTIME(14, 30, 0)
    ASSIGN ReviewHour = HOUR(ReviewTime)

    // Signed intervals reveal whether the interview followed symptom onset.
    ASSIGN DaysToInterview = DAYS(onset_date, interview_date)

    // Named FORMAT output uses the documented en-US compatibility profile; LINEBREAK is a portable LF.
    ASSIGN ReviewSummary = "Age: " & FORMAT(age, "General Number") & LINEBREAK() & "Interview: " & FORMAT(interview_date, "Short Date")

    // RECORDCOUNT excludes the Recycle Bin; ISUNIQUE checks active saved records in this form.
    ASSIGN SavedRecordCount = RECORDCOUNT()
    ASSIGN IdentifierAvailable = ISUNIQUE(id)

    // Legacy system-clock functions use bare syntax. The audit receipt records the instant and project time zone.
    ASSIGN ReviewSystemDate = SYSTEMDATE
    ASSIGN ReviewSystemTime = SYSTEMTIME

    // CURRENTUSER() is the explicit Epi Info AI account or local operator profile—not the OS login.
    ASSIGN ReviewOperator = CURRENTUSER()

    // Map > Capture Location explicitly requests permission; these bare functions only read that session context.
    ASSIGN CapturedLatitude = SYSLATITUDE
    ASSIGN CapturedLongitude = SYSLONGITUDE
    ASSIGN CapturedAltitude = SYSALTITUDE


    // RND uses an inclusive lower and exclusive upper bound; its generator, seed, and draw are audited.
    ASSIGN ReviewSampleNumber = RND(1, 97)

    // Teaching-only age standardization: PFROMZ returns a normal percentile, not a hypothesis-test p-value.
    ASSIGN AgeTeachingZ = (age - 40) / 15
    ASSIGN AgeTeachingPercentile = PFROMZ(AgeTeachingZ)

    // Safe deterministic transformations reject invalid domains instead of producing NaN or infinity.
    ASSIGN RootAge = ROUND(SQRT(age), 3)
    IF age > 0 THEN
      ASSIGN LogAge = ROUND(LN(age), 3)
    ELSE
      ASSIGN LogAge = (.)
    END-IF

    ASSIGN AdultReview = NO
    IF TXTTONUM("18") <= age AND InterviewYear >= 2026 THEN
      ASSIGN AdultReview = YES
    END-IF
  End-After
End-Record

programs.name: life-stage-by-sex
programs.source:
DEFINE AgeGroup TEXTINPUT "Age group"
RECODE Age TO AgeGroup
  LOVALUE - 4 = "0-4"
  4 - 17 = "5-17"
  17 - 44 = "18-44"
  44 - 64 = "45-64"
  64 - HIVALUE = "65+"
END
FREQ AgeGroup STRATAVAR=Sex
programs.author: Epi Info AI
programs.comment: Groups Age into five public-health life stages and runs FREQ within Sex.

runbooks.title: Foodborne investigation project tour
runbooks.description: Review the imported line list, open its saved command tour, run the visible source, and inspect the audit history.
runbooks.prerequisite: Import the Foodborne Outbreak Investigation example project. Its 96 synthetic records and saved programs are included.

steps.title: Review the line list
steps.instruction: Confirm that the imported project contains 96 synthetic foodborne investigation records. No analysis has run automatically.

steps.title: Open Classic Analysis
steps.instruction: Choose Classic Analysis from the left module rail. The project data and saved programs remain active.

steps.title: Open a saved program
steps.instruction: Select Open Pgm to see programs carried by this project package.

steps.title: Choose the command tour
steps.instruction: Choose foodborne-classic-command-tour. Review its source before opening it.

steps.title: Load visible source
steps.instruction: Select Open. Loading a program never executes it.

steps.title: Verify the program
steps.instruction: Select Verify Program and review the typed syntax result.

steps.title: Run the reviewed commands
steps.instruction: Select Run Commands only after reviewing the visible source. The output remains auditable in this browser.

steps.title: Inspect command history
steps.instruction: Open History to inspect command source, status, versions, and result summaries.

runbooks.title: Foodborne GIS investigation v0.1
runbooks.description: Relate case coordinates, neighborhood boundaries, population context, and an H3 summary in one reviewable map workflow.
runbooks.prerequisite: Import the Foodborne Outbreak Investigation example project. Its 96 synthetic records, Toledo neighborhoods, and population-density raster are included in the project package.

steps.title: Start with the investigation question
steps.instruction: Use the map to ask where reported illnesses occurred, which neighborhood context surrounds them, and whether a broad aggregate pattern is visible. The map is an investigation view, not proof of exposure or causation.

steps.title: Inspect the packaged layer stack
steps.instruction: Open Map Layers. The project package restores the named Toledo neighborhood boundary and WorldPop-derived raster as separate, checksummed assets. Layer order matters: contextual raster below boundaries and case points.

steps.title: Review reference geography
steps.instruction: Confirm the City of Toledo neighborhoods layer is present. Its polygons and name labels provide geographic context; they do not become record attributes unless a reviewed spatial join creates a derived artifact.

steps.title: Review population context
steps.instruction: Confirm the WorldPop-derived raster is present below the vector layers. It is useful visual context, but its source identifier, vintage, population concept, and units must be completed before it can support epidemiologic denominators.

steps.title: Bind records to point geography
steps.instruction: Choose Add Data Layer, then Case Cluster. Select the current foodborne form and explicitly review Latitude, Longitude, and display-label fields. Invalid WGS 84 rows are skipped rather than silently displaced.

steps.title: Review coordinate roles
steps.instruction: Latitude and Longitude are semantic coordinate roles, not merely numeric columns. Keep Latitude as Y, Longitude as X, require signed WGS 84 values, and preserve at least five decimal places in this teaching dataset.

steps.title: Inspect mapped records
steps.instruction: After selecting OK in the Case Cluster dialog, inspect the mapped-record count and fit the layer extent. A marker remains linked to its source record; the source line list remains authoritative.

steps.title: Create a derived H3 summary
steps.instruction: Choose Add Data Layer, then H3 Hexagons. H3 is a derived aggregation of the current case points, not a replacement for them. Review how resolution changes average hexagon edge length and area before adding the layer.

steps.title: Choose scale consciously
steps.instruction: Higher H3 resolutions create smaller hexagons and more local detail; lower resolutions summarize broader areas. Choose a scale appropriate to the study area and disclosure risk, then add the layer.

steps.title: Compare without conflating layers
steps.instruction: Fit Layers and compare raw points, derived H3 cells, neighborhood context, and raster context. Visibility and ordering change the presentation, not the source data or analytical result.

steps.title: Recognize the v0.1 audit boundary
steps.instruction: This runnable example preserves project assets and layer state, but the production epi-gis kernel will add reviewed plans, processing receipts, CRS diagnostics, immutable derived artifacts, and reproducible spatial joins. Those planned functions are not claimed by this walkthrough.

runbooks.title: Foodborne Check Code tour
runbooks.description: Inspect, verify, apply, and exercise the foodborne form's visible event-driven Check Code.
runbooks.prerequisite: Import the Foodborne Outbreak Investigation example project. Its form includes the Check Code source; no code runs while you inspect it in Form Designer.

steps.title: Separate Check Code from analysis programs
steps.instruction: Check Code controls data-entry events and field behavior. It is intentionally separate from the Classic Analysis .pgm7 command tour.

steps.title: Open the Check Code Editor
steps.instruction: Select Check Code to inspect the complete source stored with this form. Opening the editor does not execute it.

steps.title: Review the event program
steps.instruction: Read the DefineVariables, Form, Page, Record, and Field blocks. The case_status After event conditionally highlights and requires onset_date, then moves focus to it.

steps.title: Verify the complete source
steps.instruction: Select Verify Source. Every field and variable reference must resolve before Apply becomes available; rejected source never runs partially.

steps.title: Apply the verified Check Code
steps.instruction: Select Apply Check Code. This saves the reviewed source into the current in-browser form; it does not submit data or call an external service.

steps.title: Exercise the form events
steps.instruction: Open Enter Data. A titled Page Before Yes/No dialog demonstrates event timing and typed assignment. Choose Yes, then select OK to continue.

steps.title: Trigger conditional field behavior
steps.instruction: Enter Confirmed in Case Status and leave the field. Check Code opens the Clinical page, highlights Onset Date in yellow, makes it required, enables it, and moves focus there.

steps.title: Review the visible effect
steps.instruction: Confirm that Onset Date is highlighted and required. Choosing a different status and leaving Case Status removes the highlight and required state. Execution remains recorded in the project audit log.

steps.title: Exercise named page navigation
steps.instruction: Enter an Interview Date and leave the field. GOTOPAGE ExposureLocation closes the Clinical page event, opens the destination page event, and reveals the exposure and location fields.

steps.title: Review the active page
steps.instruction: Confirm that ExposureLocation is the active form page. Page transitions and their bounded Check Code effects are retained in project audit history.

runbooks.title: Foodborne Form Designer lab
runbooks.description: Build, validate, save, and exercise a field in the foodborne form while the runbook verifies observable completion evidence.
runbooks.prerequisite: Import the Foodborne Outbreak Investigation example project. This lab changes only its current browser working copy; reimport the project to reset it.

steps.title: Orient to the project and form
steps.instruction: Confirm that the Project Explorer shows Foodborne Outbreak Investigation and that its form is open. The runbook points to controls but does not modify the form for you.

steps.title: Add a field
steps.instruction: Select Add field. A new editable row appears at the end of Field properties.

steps.title: Define the investigation team field
steps.instruction: In the last row, set Field name to team_initials, Prompt to Investigation team initials, Type to Text, select Required, and leave Tab stop enabled. Then select Check step.

evidence.success: the field name, prompt, type, required state, and tab-stop state match the lab specification.
evidence.failure: complete all five properties in the last field row exactly as shown in the instruction.

steps.title: Open type-aware validation
steps.instruction: Select Rules in the last row. The validation choices shown must match this Text field's data type.

steps.title: Require two to five uppercase initials
steps.instruction: In Pattern (regular expression), enter ^[A-Z]{2,5}$. Select Check step; the runbook verifies the visible rule without recording its value as learner data.

evidence.success: the bounded uppercase-initials pattern is present.

steps.title: Save the field rules
steps.instruction: Select OK. This attaches the reviewed validation rule to the field in the browser working copy.

steps.title: Save the form
steps.instruction: Select Save Form to validate and persist the revised schema in this browser.

steps.title: Inspect the event-program boundary
steps.instruction: Select Check Code. Review how data-entry event logic is stored separately from field validation. Do not change or apply it during this lab.

steps.title: Confirm visible Check Code source
steps.instruction: Confirm that the editor is open and the event source remains visible and auditable. Select Check step, then close the editor with Cancel.

evidence.success: the Check Code editor is open and contains visible form event source.
evidence.failure: open Check Code and confirm that the packaged source is visible.

steps.title: Return to Form Designer
steps.instruction: Select Cancel to close the Check Code editor without replacing the current form program.

steps.title: Open Enter Data
steps.instruction: Select Enter Data to exercise the saved form. The packaged Page Before Check Code will open its titled Yes/No dialog; the runbook does not answer it or create a record for you.

steps.title: Complete the Page Before event
steps.instruction: Choose Yes in the visible Page Before dialog, then select OK. This is the Check Code action you inspected; you must provide the response yourself.

steps.title: Test the new field
steps.instruction: Find Investigation team initials, enter ABC, and leave the field. Select Check step to confirm that the saved form rendered the field and retained the entered test value. Do not save the record.

evidence.success: the saved field is present in Enter Data and contains the requested test value.
evidence.failure: enter ABC in Investigation team initials, then leave the field.

steps.title: Form Designer lab complete
steps.instruction: You added a typed field, configured validation, saved the schema, inspected Check Code, and tested the rendered control. Reimport the foodborne teaching project whenever you want a clean working copy.
